transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
Vice President J.D. Vance called out Republicans who've been criticizing fellow GOP candidate
for Ohio Governor Vivek Ramaswamy for an ad he ran against his Democratic opponent Amy
Acton.
I have to admit that I'm a little bit disgusted when I see Republicans across the country
who are whining more about that advertisement than they are about what the congressional
Democrats and other Democrats want to do to the United States of America.
The advertisement features Acton's estranged mother calling her a liar.
Acton's stepfather was charged with raping her when she was 12.
During a visit near Cincinnati today, Vance said politics is a tough business.
A new U.N. report says countries are not doing enough to cut polluting greenhouse gas emissions
and the U.S. is a big part of the problem, and appears Rebecca Hersher reports.
The U.S. saw a massive increase in how much carbon dioxide and other planet-warming pollution
it released into the atmosphere last year.
That made it an outlier among major economies, according to the report.
In 2025, the U.S. was basically tied with Russia for the most per capita emissions of
greenhouse gases, the report finds.
It was the only G20 nation where emissions increased last year.
The report blames a surge in demand for electricity, coupled with growth in burning coal in the
U.S.
The Trump administration has ordered coal-fired power plants in the U.S. to stay open longer
and rolled back limits on emissions from vehicles.
Rebecca Hersher, NPR News.
Tesla shares fell more than 3 percent in after-hours trading after the company reported flat revenue
for the third quarter, compared with the same quarter last year, NPR's Willa Rubin reports.
Most of Tesla's money comes from selling cars, especially the Model 3 and the Model Y.
And those sales dropped during the quarter, compared with the same period last year.
In a call with analysts, CEO Elon Musk didn't talk much about cars, though.
Instead, he focused on the kinds of technologies Tesla is investing a ton in, like robotaxes
and building humanoid robots.
While capital expenditures more than doubled from the same quarter last year, they were
down from the previous quarter.
Musk was also asked about his announcement on Tuesday's SpaceX earnings call that the
two companies had launched special committees to explore the possibility of merging.
But he said they weren't going to take more questions about it, and he said talking about
it was like "tap dancing through a minefield."
Willa Rubin, NPR News.
Doctors have confirmed that Pope Leo's lung cancer was localized and no further treatment
is needed.
Pope Leo returned to the Vatican on Saturday after having the lower lobe of his right lung
removed four days earlier.
The surgery confirmed he had lung adenocarcinoma, which is the most common type of lung cancer.
Major U.S. stock indexes climbed today after strong profit reports from SpaceX, Capital
One, and other big companies.
The Dow added six-tenths of a percent, and the Nasdaq climbed more than one percent.
This is NPR News from Washington.
New Mexico's Democratic Attorney General is suing Jeffrey Epstein's former attorney
and accountant, the lawsuit accuses Darren Indike and Richard Kahn of concealing the
disgraced financier's alleged sex trafficking operation at his ranch near Santa Fe.
The lawsuit also seeks to stop them from accepting any payments from Epstein's estate.
Attorney General Raul Torres accused Indike and Kahn of being aware of sexual abuse of
girls and young women at Epstein's Zorro Ranch.
North Korea plans to resume propaganda broadcasts aimed at South Korea by the end of the month.
The news comes after both sides halted this form of psychological warfare in 2025, and
NPR's Anthony Kuhn reports from Seoul.
North Korean state media quoted leader Kim Jong-un's sister Kim Yeo-jong as saying the
North will activate loudspeakers along its entire border with the South.
They also reported that Kim Yeo-jong and high-ranking military officials visited sites along the
Demilitarized Zone, or DMZ, where the North has built new fortifications.
State media quoted North Korean Marshal Park Jong-chon as telling front-line troops to
take "resolute action" if the South provokes them.
Tensions have escalated since last month when North Korean landmines exploded in the DMZ,
injuring three South Korean soldiers.
Anthony Kuhn, NPR News, Seoul.
Katherine Breed has become the first person to swim the entire length of California's
coastline.
She began the journey on July 1 from the California-Oregon border, finishing about two miles offshore
from Tijuana on Monday.
She battled storms, saw a few sharks, and braved 48-degree waters during the 100-day-long journey.
I'm Rylan Barton.
This is NPR News.

UN report says U.S. emissions surged in 2025, making it an outlier among major economies
Tesla shares fall after flat third-quarter revenue and declining car sales
Pope Leo's lung cancer confirmed localized; no further treatment needed, doctors say
